title.narrative: Provide lifesaving SRH and GBV services to persons displaced due to recent hostilities in Syria

description.narrative: Syria Country Office (SCO) plans to expand access to health and protection services to people displaced by the escalation of hostilities in Aleppo, Homs and other parts of Syria, recent returnees and host communities; this project will provide comprehensive integrated GBV and SRH services in Hama, Deir ez-Zor, and Rural Damascus. In partnership with local organizations, UNFPA will deliver integrated GBV case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services through static Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) and Integrated Mobile Teams (IMTs). The project will also provide GBV prevention and awareness sessions, along with dignity kits to mitigate GBV risks. Furthermore, the project will strengthen SRH services through local NGOs operating static facilities in Hama, Qunaitra, and Rural Damascus, addressing service gaps in areas with high humanitarian needs (OCHA severity level 3-4). Finally, the project will expand existing Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) to support the transportation cost for accessing safe delivery, SRH commodities and facilitate referrals for laboratory services and advanced maternal care through the work plan activities of the selected partners in this action.UNFPA Turkiye Cross Border (TXB) will procure, transship, and distribute 124 Inter-Agency Emergency Health Kits (IARH Kits) and 12783 RH items to 143 reproductive health facilities in NWS. The kits and supplies will cover part of the needs for a three-month period. IARH kits are intended to speed up the provision of lifesaving reproductive health services in acute humanitarian settings, ensuring the continuation of critical sexual and reproductive health service provision. The IARH kits comprise a selection of vital medications, equipment, and supplies necessary to fulfill the service goals of the minimum initial service package (MISP) for SRH. Each of the IARH kits responds to a particular reproductive health need and contains supplies calculated for a specific number of people to cover the needs of six months.The IARH kits will be procured through UNFPA’s global Supply Chain Management Unit and transshipped to NW Syria. IARH Kits and supplies will be stored in one warehouse of SAMS in Sarmada. Health facilities and distributing partners have been identified by UNFPA, in partnership with the SRH Technical Working Group (TWG). Health facilities and distributing partners have been identified by UNFPA, in partnership with the SRH TWG.In addition through two mobile units (in the form of a caravan) comprising both response and outreach team, UNFPA in partnership with Shafak, will provide GBV response and prevention services, including mental health and psychosocial support. The mobile team will also disseminate integrated messaging on GBV and SRH, conduct GBV risk assessments during dignity kit distribution and provide cash assistance in the framework of GBV case management. The two Mobile Women and Girls Safe Spaces (MWGSS) are urgently needed to address critical protection gaps in Northwest Syria. The first will serve the Aleppo countryside, targeting vulnerable areas such as Azaz, Tal Rifaat, Anadan, Haritan, Nubul, and Al-Zahraa, which host large numbers of IDPs at high risk of GBV. The second will operate in the Idleb countryside, focusing on underserved locations like Maaret Tamisrin, Saraqib, Taftanaz, and Afes, where GBV services are severely lacking. These MWGSS initiatives aim to provide life-saving GBV services and empower the most marginalized women and girls.
